meta.title: What Stockouts Actually Cost You — Lost Sales for Shopify
meta.description: Every day you’re sold out, you lose money you’ll never see. Shopify calls those quiet days low demand. Lost Sales counts them, prices them, and ranks the products to protect.

hero.badge: Lost Sales · in the lab · waitlist open
hero.headline: Sold out is costing you <accent>more than you think.</accent>
hero.subhead: Every day you’re sold out, you lose money you’ll never see. Lost Sales shows you how much.
hero.finePrint: It starts counting the day you connect. Every day before that is a day you’ll never get back.

card.days: days your best product sat at zero
card.records: systems that wrote down what it cost
card.caption: Sample figures. Shopify keeps every sale it made — nothing keeps the ones it couldn’t.

identify.title: There’s no alert for money you didn’t make.

one.statement: Your bestseller hit zero on a Tuesday. The restock landed the next Thursday.

two.statement: Shopify shows nine quiet days. It calls that low demand.
two.body: So the next order is smaller. So it sells out again.

three.statement: Nobody told you. You found out when a customer asked.
three.body: You live in your reports. You know today’s sold-out SKU.

four.statement: You have no idea what last quarter’s sold-out days cost you.
four.body: Because nothing, anywhere, wrote it down.

identify.closer: And it came out of the same cash you need for the next order.

logic.title: Every day at zero gets a dollar figure

one.title: Priced, not guessed
one.body: Every day a product sits at zero gets a dollar figure. Yours. From your run-rate, your price, your hours out. The math is on the screen — check it against your own admin.

two.title: Ranked by what it cost
two.body: You get a list, ranked by what each product cost you while it was gone.

three.title: The five you protect
three.body: You know which five you can’t afford to run out of. Not a guess. A number.

logic.footer: It starts counting the day you connect. Every day before that is a day nobody wrote down — which is exactly why the number doesn’t exist yet.

objections.title: The three reasons not to believe this — answered

one.q: “I know when I’m out of stock.”
one.a: You know today’s. You don’t know last quarter’s 31 zero-days across 14 products, or what they cost. Nobody kept that.

two.a: From data that isn’t there. Shopify doesn’t keep hours-at-zero. Once the moment passes, it’s gone. The only way to have the number is to have been counting.

three.a: Every dollar shows its math. If it doesn’t tie out to your admin, don’t trust it.

confess.title: “Those 8 zero-days weren’t low demand — they were no inventory.”
confess.sub: A plain average can’t tell the difference between “nobody wanted it” and “we had nothing to sell.” Neither can your forecast, and that’s the part that keeps costing you.

solution.title: You never lose those sales again.
solution.sub: You know exactly which products to protect — before the quarter closes, not after.
solution.withoutBody: It keeps looking like a slow week. The forecast keeps ordering less. The bestseller keeps running out. And the money keeps leaving with no record it was ever there.
solution.withBody: You know what sold out cost you. In dollars. Per product. Before the quarter closes.
